title: The Longest Path With No Equal Neighbours

concept.title: Each node keeps its two longest downward chains that are allowed to continue
body: Every node of the tree carries a letter. A path is *allowed* if no two **neighbouring nodes on it have the same letter**. Find the allowed path with the most nodes. As in the "best path with negative values" problem, every path has a **highest node**, where it comes up from one child and goes down to another.

For each node `v` let `down[v]` be the number of nodes in the longest allowed chain that starts at `v` and goes **down** (`down[v] = 1 + the best of the allowed child chains`). A child `c` can extend the chain of `v` only if its letter differs from the letter of `v`. At each node keep the **two longest** such child chains `m1 >= m2`: the longest path whose highest node is `v` has `1 + m1 + m2` nodes, and the chain returned to the parent is `1 + m1`.

body.code:
best = 1
for v in reversed(order):                   # children before parents
    best = max(best, 1 + m1[v] + m2[v])      # the path that bends at v
    chain = 1 + m1[v]                        # the chain to give to the parent
    p = parent[v]
    if p and letter[v] != letter[p]:         # only if the letters differ
        if chain > m1[p]:
            m2[p], m1[p] = m1[p], chain
        elif chain > m2[p]:
            m2[p] = chain

body: Walking the breadth-first order backwards visits every node after all its children, so no recursion is needed (the tree can be a path of 20000 nodes). Remember that the answer counts **nodes**, and a single node is always an allowed path.

statement: A tree with `n` nodes is given by the parent of each node (0 for the root), and every node has a lowercase letter. A path is allowed if no two neighbouring nodes on it have the same letter. Print the largest number of nodes of an allowed path (a single node is an allowed path).
inputFormat: The first line has `n`, the number of nodes (numbered 1 to n).
The second line has `n` numbers: for each node its parent, and 0 for the root.
The third line has a string `s` of `n` lowercase letters: `s[i]` is the letter of the node `i`.
outputFormat: Print the largest number of nodes.
constraints: The numbers describe one tree: exactly one node has the parent 0, and following parents always reaches it.
A parent can have a larger number than its child.
The tree can be a long path (depth up to n - 1).

examples.note: The letters of the nodes 1..6 are a b a c b e. The path 4-2-1 (letters c, b, a) is allowed and has 3 nodes; longer paths contain two neighbours with the same letter (the nodes 1 and 3, or 2 and 5). The answer is 3.

hints: For each node compute the longest downward chain whose neighbours have different letters.
A child with the same letter as its parent cannot extend the chain of the parent.
Keep the two best chains at every node: they give the best path bent at the node, 1 + m1 + m2.

explanation: In reverse breadth-first order every node already has the chains of its children. It keeps the two longest chains coming from children with a different letter; the path bent at the node has 1 + m1 + m2 nodes, and 1 + m1 is offered to the parent.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
par = list(map(int, input().split()))
s = input().strip()

kids = [[] for _ in range(n + 1)]
root = 0
for v in range(1, n + 1):
    if par[v - 1] == 0:
        root = v
    else:
        kids[par[v - 1]].append(v)
order = [root]
for v in order:
    order.extend(kids[v])
m1 = [0] * (n + 1)
m2 = [0] * (n + 1)
best = 1
for v in reversed(order):
    best = max(best, 1 + m1[v] + m2[v])
    chain = 1 + m1[v]
    p = par[v - 1]
    if p != 0 and s[v - 1] != s[p - 1]:
        if chain > m1[p]:
            m2[p] = m1[p]
            m1[p] = chain
        elif chain > m2[p]:
            m2[p] = chain
print(best)
